data.narrative:
Elroy Air, a Series B autonomous drone company founded by David Merrill and Clint Cope, is valued at $800M post-money following $116M in total capital raised. The Drones & Autonomous sector comprises 8 private peers (including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro) and no public comparables, limiting traditional benchmarking approaches.

Stage-progression analysis, the only triangulation method applicable to this dataset, uses a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B to later-stage transitions applied to the $800M last post-money valuation. This yields an implied valuation of $1.5B. A peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Drones & Autonomous cohort; the six identified sector peers lack sufficient density in overlapping stage and valuation bands to produce a reliable median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.3B to $1.7B, with a median of $1.5B. This range reflects typical Series B progression dynamics but carries material uncertainty given the reliance on a single method and the sector's thin peer coverage at comparable stages. Key risks to valuation include the nascent commercialization of autonomous cargo platforms, regulatory variability across geographies, and the substantial capital intensity of this segment. Further validation would benefit from closer monitoring of capital efficiency metrics relative to the identified peer set as they progress toward Series C and beyond.
